propositions: Cancelled ACLI link-delete commands exit non-zero with 'command cancelled' stderr but are counted toward links_applied, fabricating success and preventing failure detection.

The except-CalledProcessError arm in _update_one_dispatch_links increments links_applied unconditionally rather than distinguishing idempotent 404/409 races from deterministic cancellations, silencing logs and hiding the defect.

ACLI link subcommands prompt for confirmation by default; with stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL they read EOF and fail deterministically every pass, producing permanent silent divergence rather than transient races.

ACLI 1.3.19-stable (the fleet's cached version) accepts --yes flag on both 'workitem link create' and 'workitem link delete' subcommands to skip confirmation, matching the precedent already used on 'workitem delete' (bug 3256).
The narrowed idempotent check must match failure markers on both stderr AND stdout (not stderr-only) to correctly classify concurrent-removal races, following the precedent in acli.py:739-742.
A new links_failed counter reported in batch_outcome output enables the silent-noop canary to distinguish benign concurrent removals from genuine cancellation failures.
